ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A small ball of mass m is tied by light strings a and b respectively to point B and point A of a light thin rod, as shown in the figure. String a makes an angle θ with the horizontal direction, and string b is in the horizontal direction and has length l. When the light rod rotates uniformly about the axis AB with angular velocity ω, the small ball performs uniform circular motion in a horizontal plane. Then which of the following statements is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: When the angular velocity $\omega>\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{gcot}\theta}l}$, string b will have tension

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A small ball of mass m is tied by light strings a and b respectively to point B and point A of a light thin rod, as shown in the figure. String a makes an angle θ with the horizontal direction, and string b is in the horizontal direction and has length l. When the light rod rotates uniformly about the axis AB with angular velocity ω, the small ball performs uniform circular motion in a horizontal plane. Question: when the angular velocity ω satisfies what condition will string b have tension?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When the angular velocity $\omega>\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{gcot}\theta}l}$, string b will have tension
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure there is a vertical light rod; near the upper end of the rod it is labeled B, and near the lower end it is labeled A. AB is the vertical rotation axis, and angular velocity ω is marked beside it. The small ball is on the left side of the rod. The inclined string a connects from the small ball to point B, and the inclined string a makes an angle θ with the horizontal direction; the horizontal string b connects from the small ball to point A, and its horizontal length is marked as l. Then reason: let the tension of the inclined string a be T_a, and the tension of the horizontal string b be T_b. The small ball performs uniform circular motion in a horizontal plane, and there is no acceleration in the vertical direction, so the vertical direction is balanced: T_a sinθ = mg. The resultant force in the horizontal direction pointing toward the rotation axis provides the centripetal force; from the horizontal string b in the figure, it can be known that the radius of the circular motion is l, so T_a cosθ + T_b = mω^2 l. To determine when string b just begins to have tension, take the critical state T_b = 0. At this time T_a = mg/sinθ. Substituting into the horizontal centripetal-force equation gives: (mg/sinθ)cosθ = mω^2 l, that is, mg cotθ = mω^2 l, so the critical angular velocity is ω0 = sqrt(g cotθ / l). When the angular velocity continues to increase, the required centripetal force is greater than the horizontal component of the inclined string a, and string b must provide additional pulling force, so the condition for string b to have tension is ω > sqrt(g cotθ / l).
